follow_up.blocking_question: Which MarkerInitializationError value, if any, must represent target-name UTF-16 encoding or ctypes rename-buffer construction failures after CreateFileW succeeds?

findings.rationale: A successful CreateFileW call is followed by target-name encoding and ctypes buffer construction before the current try/finally begins. An exception in that window can leak the HANDLE and escape instead of returning an initialization result. The Contract requires normal initialization failures to be returned as MarkerInitializationError values, but explicitly does not require programming errors or violated Python-level preconditions to be converted. It does not classify encoding, allocation, or buffer-construction failures at this boundary, so an exact public failure mapping cannot be inferred.
required_action: After Contract clarification, begin HANDLE protection immediately after CreateFileW success and keep every subsequent operation through SetFileInformationByHandle inside that try/finally lifecycle.
Always call CloseHandle in the finally block for a successfully acquired HANDLE.
Map only the failure categories explicitly classified by the clarified Contract; do not introduce a broad exception-to-MarkerInitializationError conversion.

follow_up.baseline_handling: Create a new Frozen Test and new approved Baseline version; do not modify v0.2.
follow_up.process_question: The Test Strategy requires a new approved Baseline version when Test input or Acceptance Criteria changes, but does not define TEST_BASELINE_COVERAGE_EXTENSION as a formal classification.
follow_up.red_rationale: Test Strategy section 2.2 permits red_check_required=false for regression additions to an existing Capability and prohibits forcing an artificial failure where meaningful RED cannot be constructed. The production branch already implements the specified mismatch result, so manufacturing RED would require intentionally breaking verified behavior.

findings.rationale: Contract section 7.4 requires a valid reload result whose DataRootMarker differs from the intended marker to return MarkerReloadVerificationFailed. Production contains this comparison, but Frozen Test v0.2 does not exercise the valid-but-different branch.
required_action: After process clarification and Human approval, add a separate Frozen test under a new Baseline version.
Inject a successful reload that returns a valid LoadedDataRootMarker whose marker differs from the intended marker in at least one Contract field.
Assert MarkerReloadVerificationFailed and assert that the published final target remains present and is neither deleted nor repaired.
Record red_check_required=false with the Test Strategy section 2.2 regression-coverage rationale; do not create synthetic RED.
